page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-64-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine belonging to the z4d server family. Built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, this instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs and 504.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per core. The server does not include any GPU accelerators, focusing its hardware profile entirely on high-capacity compute, memory, and local storage resources.

A defining characteristic of this configuration is its integrated local storage subsystem. It is equipped with 15,032 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across four local drives. This massive local storage capacity is bundled directly with the instance, providing high-throughput and low-latency data access. However, the lack of GPU acceleration makes it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated machine learning or graphics rendering workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the z4d-highmem-64-standardlssd offers high resource density by combining substantial memory capacity with extensive local NVMe storage on a single node. This hardware profile is designed for data-intensive workloads that require rapid access to large datasets. Appropriate workloads include large-scale databases, data warehousing, real-time analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that benefit from localized high-speed storage.
